thread:
lee: heads up — ap-northeast-1 edge egress is hitting ephemeral port exhaustion right now, multiple pods failing outbound to model-store (443). saw spike ~08:12 UTC.
marta: seeing a ton of TIME_WAIT on the sidecars, connections to s3/model-bucket keep tearing. symptoms: 502 from edge-proxy then RSTs.
raj: confirmed NAT GW 3/4 in us-east-1? wait this is ap-northeast-1 — ok NAT gateway byte/conn limits reached per-AZ. Cloud metrics show SNAT port pool exhausted on a couple of AZs.
ashley: this is from new batch of model pullers after a deploy — nodes pulled concurrently (~1200) to warm cache. we bumped parallelism to speed up cold-starts.
sam: quick checks: run `ss -tan state TIME-WAIT | wc -l` on a sidecar, and `aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics` for NATActiveConnections.
lee: ran quick `ss` — on one sidecar: 18k TIME_WAIT, local ports ~1024-32767. huge reuse pressure.
ops-bot: incident-notice: egress-port-exhaustion triggered alert (egress_port_utilization > 95%) for ap-northeast-1-edge (runbook v3).
marta: short term mitigation ideas: 1) throttle model pullers (reduce concurrency to 4 per node), 2) enable S3 VPC endpoint for model-store to avoid NAT, 3) add a small pool of NAT instances per-AZ to increase port space.
raj: adding NAT instances buys ports but is operationally heavier. S3 VPC endpoint is immediate and cheap, but model-store is a cross-account bucket served via CloudFront currently so needs IAM/endpoint policy work.
ashley: we can flip deploy to use the per-AZ cache service (we have an internal http cache) instead of direct S3 pulls — that'll cut egress by ~90%. quick patch: set `MODEL_FETCH_PARALLEL=2` and fallback to cache.
sam: also consider TCP tweaks on sidecars: increase `net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range` to `15000 61000` and `net.ipv4.tcp_fin_timeout=15` and set `tcp_tw_reuse=1` — buys some headroom. note: these are kernel-level and require node image change.
lee: cost tradeoff: adding 1 NAT Gateway per AZ ~ $0.045/hr + data charges; NAT instances cheaper but ops cost. prefer VPC endpoints + throttle + kernel tweaks for now.
raj: long term: implement connection pooling in the sidecar so we reuse upstream sockets (keepalive + HTTP/2) and/or put a dedicated outbound proxy (redirect all egress through an NLB->haproxy fleet with long-lived connections). that reduces ephemeral churn.
marta: immediate plan: 1) rollback parallelism bump (ashley), 2) open PR to enable model-store VPC endpoint whitelist (raj + sec), 3) schedule node boot image change with sysctls (sam), 4) temp provision 2 NAT instances in affected AZs if exhaustion > 98% after throttling.
ashley: rolling back patch now (rolling deploy) — setting MODEL_FETCH_PARALLEL=2 and disabling parallel warmers. will post deploy id.
lee: raj, can you start the VPC endpoint policy draft? need it today. sam, can you prep an AMI change with the tcp sysctls?
raj: on it. will ping sec for policy and add CloudFront origin check.
sam: prepping AMI diff. will test net.ipv4 settings in staging. estimated 2 hours to build/test.
ops-bot: update: runbook action 1 executed: throttle applied by release 2026-03-18_08:25.
marta: monitoring: port utilization dropped from 98% to 64% within 8 minutes after throttling and VPC endpoint staging rules. traffic errors reduced.
lee: ok next: schedule a follow up in 2 hours to decide on NAT instance provisioning if it creeps back up. also add a short-term grafana panel showing ephemeral port headroom per-AZ.
ashley: deploy id 2026-03-18-398 applied. warming concurrency reduced.
raj: started endpoint PR: https://git.internal/rj/vpc-endpoint-modelstore. added sample policy and test harness.
sam: AMI build passed unit net tests. will run staging boot in 30m.
marta: thumbs up. thanks everyone — documenting final mitigations in runbook and will close the alert if stable for 30m. :thumbsup:
